content_preview.title: CISA Adds N-able N-central Auth Bypass to KEV Catalog After an Incomplete Patch Let Attackers Back In
content_preview.summary: CVE-2026-18577, an authentication bypass in N-able's N-central RMM platform, is under active exploitation and now carries a federal patch deadline of August 6.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added a high-severity N-able N-central vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on August 3, 2026, following reports of active exploitation in the wild, according to [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/08/cisa-adds-exploited-n-able-n-central.html). The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-18577, is the result of an incomplete patch for an earlier authentication bypass, CVE-2026-18556, according to [NVD](...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) with clear prose and appropriate technical depth. The 'incomplete patch let attackers back in' framing is a reasonable emphasis choice, but it describes the same underlying mechanism already reported in the published PR #2128 article, not a distinct story.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 7 snapshots in sources/2026-08/cisa-adds-n-able-n-central-auth-bypass-to-kev-catalog-after-an-incomplete-patch-let-attackers-back-in/ (source-0 BleepingComputer [Archive.org fallback], source-1 TheHackerNews 'CISA Adds...', source-2 TheHackerNews 'N-able Says Attackers Take Over...', source-3 N-able blog [Archive.org fallback], source-4 Huntress, source-5 NVD, source-6 CISA KEV JSON feed). Verified: CVE-2026-18577/CVSS 8.1 (v3.1)/8.2 (v4.0) and 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556' language (source-5 NVD, matches CISA source-6 shortDescription); CISA KEV dateAdded 2026-08-03 and dueDate 2026-08-06 (source-6, matches article); hotfix build 2026.3.1.7 released Aug 2 (source-0, source-2); Take Control pivot and Cloudflare-tunnel persistence mechanism (source-3 N-able blog, source-2); the 'MSP Support' default-username detail (source-2); the NordVPN/Mullvad IP attribution quotes and the exact IPs 87.249.138[.]34 / 37.19.210[.]32 (source-4 Huntress, quoted verbatim); the 'nine organisations under one partner account, one endpoint each' / 'enumerating running processes' detail attributed to The Hacker News' email exchange with Huntress (source-2, verified verbatim — this submission correctly attributes it to TheHackerNews rather than directly to Huntress); the 28.6% self-hosted-unpatched figure as of Aug 3 2:15pm ET (source-4 Huntress). One fabricated claim found: the first paragraph of 'What We Know' states 'N-able's Adlumin managed detection and response solution detected unusual activity in a customer's environment on July 31, 2026, which led the company to discover a threat actor actively exploiting a zero-day vulnerability on an N-central server,' citing N-able's own security update (source-3). The actual N-able blog snapshot (source-3) contains no such claim — 'Adlumin' appears only twice, both in unrelated site-navigation product menus ('Adlumin SecOps', 'Threat Hunting Adlumin'), and the word 'zero-day' does not appear anywhere in the page. The blog's own 'Background' section instead attributes discovery to 'an increase in licensing issues for our on-premises N-central customers' on July 31, 2026, which was unusually high in volume and prompted engineering/security teams to investigate, leading to the discovery on Aug 2 that a previously-patched vulnerability (CVE-2026-18556) had an unblocked alternate exploitation path. This is a fabricated causal narrative and a fabricated attribution, not a paraphrase — and it is the identical fabrication pattern (Adlumin MDR detecting 'unusual activity' leading to discovery of a 'zero-day') already flagged and REJECTed in three sibling submissions on this same story earlier today (#2129, #2131, #2133; e.g. review at src/content/reviews/2026-08/2026-08-05T09-19-11Z_cisa-adds-exploited-n-able-n-central-authenticatio_review.json), confirming this is a recurring hallucination the contributor bot generates for this specific event rather than an isolated error.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Aside from the fabricated Adlumin/zero-day detection narrative, all other checked specifics — CVSS scores, KEV dates, hotfix version, IOCs, IP attributions, the nine-organizations figure, and the 28.6% unpatched figure — are accurately sourced. One additional minor note: source-0 (BleepingComputer)'s own snapshot text contains an apparent typo, referring to the earlier vulnerability as 'CVE-2026-18576' in one place; the submission correctly uses 'CVE-2026-18556' throughout, matching NVD (source-5) and CISA (source-6), so this is not an error introduced by the bot.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; no editorializing or sensationalism observed.
editor_notes.originality: REJECT-determining issue, checked against the now-updated archive per instructions. This submission covers the exact same underlying event as the already-published article at src/content/articles/2026-08/05-cisa-orders-federal-agencies-to-patch-actively-exploited-n-able-n-central-authentication-bypass.md (PR #2128, merged and published earlier the same day, 2026-08-05). Both articles cover CVE-2026-18577, the CVSS 8.2 score, the 'incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556' characterization, the Take Control pivot mechanism, the Cloudflare-tunnel persistence technique, N-able's 2026.3.1.7 hotfix, and CISA's KEV addition with the August 6 federal deadline. Sources overlap substantially: 5 of this submission's 7 sources (TheHackerNews 'CISA Adds...', N-able's blog, Huntress, NVD, CISA's KEV feed) are identical URLs to sources used in the published article. The 'incomplete patch let attackers back in' headline framing and the second TheHackerNews follow-up article (source-2, the nine-organizations detail) are the only genuinely new elements versus #2128, and they are incremental detail on the same event rather than a distinct newsworthy angle or development. It is the same story, same day, same CVE pair, told from largely the same set of facts.
concerns: Duplicate of already-published article (PR #2128 / src/content/articles/2026-08/05-cisa-orders-federal-agencies-to-patch-actively-exploited-n-able-n-central-authentication-bypass.md) covering the same CVE-2026-18577/CVE-2026-18556 N-central auth-bypass event, same day.

Fabricated quote and detection narrative attributed to N-able's blog ('Adlumin MDR solution detected unusual activity... discover a threat actor actively exploiting a zero-day vulnerability') not found in source-3 or any of the other 6 cited source snapshots; the real N-able blog attributes discovery to a spike in licensing errors, not an MDR/Adlumin detection or a zero-day.

This is the fourth submission today on this exact story to contain this same fabricated Adlumin/zero-day narrative (after #2129, #2131, #2133, all REJECTed) — a recurring, event-specific hallucination pattern in the contributor bot, not an isolated slip.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The controlling issue is duplication: this submission covers the same underlying story as the already-published PR #2128 article on the same CVE, published earlier the same day, with 5 of 7 identical sources and no genuinely distinct angle. Independent of the duplication, source verification also found the same fabricated Adlumin MDR/zero-day detection narrative already identified and REJECTed in three sibling submissions on this exact event — the claim appears in the lead paragraph of 'What We Know' and is unsupported by N-able's actual blog post or any other cited source. Either finding alone would preclude a clean APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS (duplication cannot be honestly corrected into non-duplication; a fabricated causal narrative this early in the article is not a single recoverable specific, and is part of a now-established pattern across four submissions). Per the v3.9.0 workflow this is a REJECT — the PR is closed and the work is not eligible for rewrite.
